title: The end of the office
paragraphs: For many white-collar workers around the world, the recent pandemic has meant having to work from home. Their usual office location has been out of bounds. This means different working practices, which have advantages and disadvantages for employees. But the big question is, will they ever see their offices again?

Home working has made people realise what tasks they can perform at home, rather than enduring a commute to the office to do the same thing. It has given them more time with the family; they’ve been sleeping better and have saved money by not travelling or buying lunches on the go. And recent research suggests the majority of people working from home are just as productive.

For some people, this could be a permanent arrangement. In the UK, fifty of the biggest employers questioned by the BBC, have said they have no plans to return all staff to the office full-time in the near future. Of course, one main reason is that firms couldn’t see a way of accommodating large numbers of staff while social distancing regulations were still in place. But the BBC also heard from some smaller businesses who are deciding to abandon their offices altogether.

Other bigger companies are also looking at shutting offices to save money as many jobs can be performed remotely. Peter Cheese, head of the Chartered Institute of Personnel and Development, told the BBC: “We’re at a moment of real change in the world of work, driven by big existential crises.”

But this isn’t great news for everyone. Some employees can feel isolated at home, and there’s less opportunity to network or learn from other people, especially if they’re a new recruit. Also, city centres may suffer most from a change in working habits. Shops and cafes rely on the footfall of office workers, and without them, they face closure.
The future is still uncertain, which is why it may be too early to say where our desks will be permanently located. But the office of the future may be your home.

vocabulary.entry: white-collar worker /ˌwaɪt ˈkɒlə wɜːkə/ n. 白领员工
vocabulary.example: She has been a white-collar worker in a financial firm for five years.
vocabulary.translation: 她在一家金融公司做白领员工已经五年了。

vocabulary.entry: pandemic /pænˈdemɪk/ n. （全国或全球性）流行病
vocabulary.example: The country took strict measures to deal with the pandemic.
vocabulary.translation: 该国采取了严格措施应对这场流行病。

vocabulary.entry: work from home /wɜːk frəm həʊm/ 居家办公
vocabulary.example: More people choose to work from home to avoid the rush hour.
vocabulary.translation: 越来越多的人选择居家办公，以避开交通高峰期。

vocabulary.entry: office location /ˈɒfɪs ləʊˈkeɪʃn/ n. 办公地点
vocabulary.example: The company is considering a new office location in the suburbs.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司正在考虑在郊区选一个新的办公地点。

vocabulary.entry: out of bounds /aʊt ɒv baʊndz/ 禁止入内
vocabulary.example: The construction area is out of bounds to the public.
vocabulary.translation: 这个施工区域禁止公众入内。

vocabulary.entry: working practice /ˈwɜːkɪŋ ˈpræktɪs/ n. 工作模式
vocabulary.example: The manager introduced a new working practice to improve efficiency.
vocabulary.translation: 经理引入了一种新的工作模式来提高效率。

vocabulary.entry: employee /ɪmˈplɔɪiː/ n. 雇员；员工
vocabulary.example: The company provides training opportunities for every employee.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司为每位员工都提供培训机会。

vocabulary.entry: commute /kəˈmjuːt/ n. 通勤；上下班路程
vocabulary.example: His daily commute takes about 40 minutes by subway.
vocabulary.translation: 他每天坐地铁通勤大约需要四十分钟。

vocabulary.entry: on the go /ɒn ðə ɡəʊ/ 忙个不停；四处奔走
vocabulary.example: She eats breakfast on the go when she is late for work.
vocabulary.translation: 上班快要迟到的时候，她就边走边吃早餐。

vocabulary.entry: productive /prəˈdʌktɪv/ adj. 有效率的；多产的
vocabulary.example: They had a productive discussion and solved many problems.
vocabulary.translation: 他们进行了一次富有成效的讨论，解决了诸多问题。

vocabulary.entry: permanent arrangement /ˈpɜːmənənt əˈreɪndʒmənt/ n. 长期安排
vocabulary.example: This is not a permanent arrangement and we will adjust it later.
vocabulary.translation: 这不是长期安排，我们之后会做出调整。

vocabulary.entry: employer /ɪmˈplɔɪə/ n. 雇主；老板
vocabulary.example: The employer is responsible for the safety of the workplace.
vocabulary.translation: 雇主对工作场所的安全负有责任。

vocabulary.entry: full-time /ˌfʊl ˈtaɪm/ adj. 全职的
vocabulary.example: She got a full-time job in a law firm after graduation.
vocabulary.translation: 她毕业后在一家律师事务所找到了一份全职工作。

vocabulary.entry: accommodate /əˈkɒmədeɪt/ v. 容纳；为……提供空间
vocabulary.example: The hall can accommodate up to 500 people.
vocabulary.translation: 这个大厅最多可以容纳五百人。

vocabulary.entry: social distancing regulation /ˈsəʊʃl ˈdɪstənsɪŋ ˌreɡjuˈleɪʃn/ n. 社交距离规定
vocabulary.example: The government issued a new social distancing regulation last week.
vocabulary.translation: 政府上周颁布了一项新的社交距离规定。

vocabulary.entry: small business /smɔːl ˈbɪznəs/ n. 小型企业
vocabulary.example: The local government offers support to small business.
vocabulary.translation: 当地政府为小型企业提供扶持。

vocabulary.entry: abandon /əˈbændən/ v. 放弃；舍弃
vocabulary.example: He had to abandon his plan due to lack of funding.
vocabulary.translation: 由于资金不足，他不得不放弃自己的计划。

vocabulary.entry: big company /bɪɡ ˈkʌmpəni/ n. 大型企业
vocabulary.example: Many graduates dream of working for a big company.
vocabulary.translation: 许多毕业生都梦想进入大型企业工作。

vocabulary.entry: remotely /rɪˈməʊtli/ adv. 远程地
vocabulary.example: The technician can fix the computer problem remotely.
vocabulary.translation: 技术人员可以远程解决这个电脑故障。

vocabulary.entry: existential crisis /ˌeɡzɪˈstenʃl ˈkraɪsɪs/ n. 生存危机
vocabulary.example: The industry is facing an existential crisis because of the new policy.
vocabulary.translation: 受新政策影响，该行业正面临生存危机。

vocabulary.entry: isolated /ˈaɪsəleɪtɪd/ adj. 孤立的；孤独的
vocabulary.example: Living in a remote area, she felt a bit isolated sometimes.
vocabulary.translation: 住在偏远地区，她有时会感到有些孤独。

vocabulary.entry: footfall /ˈfʊtfɔːl/ n. 客流量
vocabulary.example: The shopping mall has seen an increase in footfall during the holiday.
vocabulary.translation: 假期期间，这家购物中心的客流量有所增加。

sentences.english: For many white-collar workers around the world, the recent pandemic has meant having to work from home.
sentences.chinese: 对于全球许多白领员工而言，近年来的疫情意味着他们不得不居家办公。

sentences.english: Their usual office location has been out of bounds.
sentences.chinese: 他们平日里的办公地点已经禁止入内。

sentences.english: This means different working practices, which have advantages and disadvantages for employees.
sentences.chinese: 这意味着迥然不同的工作模式，对员工而言各有利弊。

sentences.english: But the big question is, will they ever see their offices again?
sentences.chinese: 但一个关键问题是：他们还会重返办公室吗？

sentences.english: Home working has made people realise what tasks they can perform at home, rather than enduring a commute to the office to do the same thing.
sentences.chinese: 居家办公让人们意识到，有些工作完全可以在家完成，不必忍受通勤之苦跑去办公室做同样的事。

sentences.english: It has given them more time with the family; they’ve been sleeping better and have saved money by not travelling or buying lunches on the go.
sentences.chinese: 居家办公让他们有了更多陪伴家人的时间，睡眠质量也有所提升，同时还省下了通勤费用和外出买午餐的开支。

sentences.english: And recent research suggests the majority of people working from home are just as productive.
sentences.chinese: 近期研究表明，大多数居家办公的人，工作效率和在办公室时不相上下。

sentences.english: For some people, this could be a permanent arrangement.
sentences.chinese: 对有些人来说，居家办公可能会成为一种长期安排。

sentences.english: In the UK, fifty of the biggest employers questioned by the BBC, have said they have no plans to return all staff to the office full-time in the near future.
sentences.chinese: 在英国，英国广播公司调查的五十家大型企业均表示，近期不打算让所有员工全职返回办公室办公。

sentences.english: Of course, one main reason is that firms couldn’t see a way of accommodating large numbers of staff while social distancing regulations were still in place.
sentences.chinese: 当然，一个主要原因是，在社交距离规定仍然生效的情况下，企业无法找到合适的办法来容纳大量员工办公。

sentences.english: But the BBC also heard from some smaller businesses who are deciding to abandon their offices altogether.
sentences.chinese: 但英国广播公司也了解到，一些小型企业正决定彻底放弃办公场所。

sentences.english: Other bigger companies are also looking at shutting offices to save money as many jobs can be performed remotely.
sentences.chinese: 其他大型企业也在考虑关闭办公场所来节省开支，因为许多工作都可以远程完成。

sentences.english: Peter Cheese, head of the Chartered Institute of Personnel and Development, told the BBC: “We’re at a moment of real change in the world of work, driven by big existential crises.”
sentences.chinese: 英国特许人事与发展协会负责人彼得·奇斯向英国广播公司表示：“在重大生存危机的推动下，我们正处于职场发生真正变革的时刻。”

sentences.english: But this isn’t great news for everyone.
sentences.chinese: 但这对所有人而言并非都是好消息。

sentences.english: Some employees can feel isolated at home, and there’s less opportunity to network or learn from other people, especially if they’re a new recruit.
sentences.chinese: 有些员工在家办公会感到孤立无援，而且建立人脉或向他人学习的机会也会减少，新员工尤其如此。

sentences.english: Also, city centres may suffer most from a change in working habits.
sentences.chinese: 此外，工作习惯的改变可能会对市中心造成最严重的冲击。

sentences.english: Shops and cafes rely on the footfall of office workers, and without them, they face closure.
sentences.chinese: 商店和咖啡馆都依赖白领员工带来的客流量，失去了这些客源，它们就面临着倒闭的风险。

sentences.english: The future is still uncertain, which is why it may be too early to say where our desks will be permanently located.
sentences.chinese: 未来仍充满不确定性，因此现在断言我们的办公桌会长期放置在何处还为时过早。

sentences.english: But the office of the future may be your home.
sentences.chinese: 但未来的办公室，或许就是你的家。
